name: Git
description: Version control system for tracking changes to code.
why: Newer than the Apple-bundled git and gets updates through Homebrew.

name: GitHub CLI
description: Work with GitHub pull requests, issues and repos from the terminal.
why: Also handles GitHub login and uploading your SSH key in one step.

name: Visual Studio Code
description: Free, extensible code editor with a huge extension ecosystem.
why: The default editor for most languages; great Python, JS and remote/container support.

name: iTerm2
description: Feature-rich replacement for the built-in Terminal app.
why: Split panes, search, profiles and a hotkey drop-down window.

name: Ghostty
description: Fast, GPU-accelerated native terminal.
why: Very fast and minimal with sensible defaults; a modern alternative to iTerm2.

name: Warp
description: Terminal with IDE-style editing and built-in AI command help.
why: Friendly for people newer to the command line.

name: OrbStack
description: Lightweight Docker and Linux VM runtime for macOS.
why: Runs Docker containers using much less CPU, memory and battery than Docker Desktop.

name: Docker Desktop
description: The official Docker app for building and running containers.
why: Use it if your company standardizes on it. Note: needs a paid licence at larger companies.

name: uv
description: Extremely fast Python package and project manager.
why: Replaces pip, venv, pyenv and pipx with one tool; installs Python versions for you.

name: fnm (Node.js versions)
description: Fast Node.js version manager.
why: Lets you switch Node versions per project. After install run: fnm install --lts.

name: jq
description: Command-line JSON processor.
why: Filter and pretty-print JSON from APIs and log files.

name: ripgrep
description: Very fast recursive text search (the rg command).
why: Searches whole codebases in milliseconds and respects .gitignore.

name: fzf
description: Fuzzy finder for files, command history and more.
why: Ctrl+R becomes a searchable history of every command you have run.

name: bat
description: cat with syntax highlighting and line numbers.
why: Makes reading files in the terminal much easier.

name: eza
description: Modern ls with colours, icons and git status.
why: Easier-to-read directory listings.

name: tree
description: Shows a folder's contents as a tree.
why: Quick way to see or share a project's structure.

name: wget
description: Downloads files from the web on the command line.
why: Lots of install instructions assume it; macOS only ships curl.

name: htop
description: Interactive process viewer for the terminal.
why: A more readable top: see what is using your CPU and memory.

name: Bruno
description: Open-source API client that stores requests as files in your repo.
why: Like Postman, but offline-first and git-friendly.

name: Postman
description: Popular app for building and testing HTTP APIs.
why: Use it if your team shares Postman workspaces and collections.

name: JetBrains Toolbox
description: Installs and updates JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm...).
why: The easiest way to manage JetBrains IDEs if you prefer them over VS Code.

name: HTTPie
description: User-friendly command-line HTTP client for testing APIs and web services.
why: Colorized terminal output, JSON support, and simpler syntax than curl for API debugging.

name: Starship
description: Fast, customizable prompt for any shell showing git status and environment versions.
why: Provides immediate context about your repository and tool versions; requires one eval line in ~/.zshrc.

name: Ruff
description: Extremely fast Python linter and code formatter written in Rust.
why: Replaces Flake8, Black, isort and Bandit with 10-100x faster execution and drop-in compatibility.

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's coding agent: reads your project, edits files and runs commands from the terminal.
why: Hand it whole tasks (fix this bug, add this feature) and review the changes. Run claude in a project folder; needs a Claude account.

name: Codex
description: OpenAI's coding agent that runs in your terminal.
why: Pick this if you use ChatGPT; sign in with your ChatGPT account and run codex in a project.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source coding agent for the terminal.
why: Generous free tier with a Google account; run gemini in a project.

name: OpenCode
description: Open-source terminal coding agent that works with many model providers, including local models.
why: Use one agent with whichever model you like, even one running on your Mac through Ollama.

name: Aider
description: AI pair programming in your terminal that commits each change to Git.
why: Every edit lands as a Git commit, so it's easy to review or undo. Works with cloud and local models.

name: Cline
description: Open-source coding agent for complex, multi-step work, from the terminal.
why: Bring your own API key or local model; popular with VS Code users who want the same agent in the terminal.

name: Qwen Code
description: Coding agent tuned for Alibaba's open-weight Qwen coder models.
why: A good match if you want to code with open-weight models.

name: Cursor
description: AI-first code editor built on VS Code.
why: Same extensions and keybindings as VS Code, with built-in AI chat, edits and agents.

name: Claude
description: Anthropic's Claude desktop app for chat, writing and analysis.
why: Quicker than a browser tab, and can connect to apps and files on your Mac.

name: ChatGPT
description: OpenAI's ChatGPT desktop app.
why: Open it from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut and ask about what's on screen.

name: Ollama
description: The easiest way to run open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral...) on your Mac.
why: Private, offline and free; uses your Apple Silicon GPU. Start it with brew services start ollama, then ollama run qwen3.

name: LM Studio
description: Desktop app to find, download and chat with open-weight models.
why: The point-and-click way to run local models; also serves them to other apps through an OpenAI-compatible API.

name: Jan
description: Open-source, offline ChatGPT-style app for local models.
why: A friendly chat window for models that never leave your Mac.

name: Msty
description: Chat app that mixes local and online models side by side.
why: Compare answers from a local model and a cloud model in one place.

name: llama.cpp
description: The fast C/C++ engine behind many local-model apps, with a CLI and a local server.
why: For tinkerers: run any GGUF model directly, e.g. llama-server -hf <model>.

name: MLX-LM
description: Apple's MLX framework for running and fine-tuning models on Apple Silicon.
why: Often the fastest way to run models on an M-series Mac, and lets you fine-tune small models locally.

name: Hugging Face CLI
description: Download models and datasets from Hugging Face with the hf command.
why: Hugging Face is where open-weight models are published; this fetches them for llama.cpp, MLX and others.

name: LLM
description: Simon Willison's command-line tool for prompting cloud and local models.
why: Pipe files and command output into a model, and keep a searchable log of every prompt.

name: Google Chrome
description: Google's web browser.
why: Best DevTools and website compatibility; syncs bookmarks from your old laptop.

name: Firefox
description: Mozilla's open-source, privacy-focused browser.
why: Good for privacy and for testing sites in a second browser engine.

name: Arc
description: Chromium browser with vertical tabs and separate Spaces.
why: Keeps work and personal tabs organized; uses Chrome extensions.

name: Brave
description: Chromium browser with built-in ad and tracker blocking.
why: Chrome compatibility with stronger privacy by default.

name: Slack
description: Team chat with channels and huddles.
why: Standard workplace chat for most tech teams.

name: Zoom
description: Video meetings and webinars.
why: Most external meetings and interviews use Zoom. Installing it asks for your Mac password.

name: Microsoft Teams
description: Microsoft's chat and meetings app.
why: Needed if your company or school runs on Microsoft 365. Asks for your Mac password.

name: WhatsApp
description: Desktop app for WhatsApp messages and calls.
why: Type messages with a real keyboard; linked to your phone.

name: Discord
description: Voice, video and text communities.
why: Many open-source projects and dev communities live here.

name: Telegram
description: Fast cloud-based messaging app.
why: Syncs across all devices without needing your phone online.

name: Rectangle
description: Snap windows to halves, thirds and corners with keyboard shortcuts.
why: macOS window management is basic; this makes split-screen work effortless.

name: Raycast
description: Spotlight replacement: launcher, clipboard history, snippets and extensions.
why: Open apps, search files, do calculations and run scripts without touching the mouse.

name: Alfred
description: Long-standing launcher with powerful workflows (Powerpack is paid).
why: Pick this instead of Raycast if you prefer a one-time purchase.

name: 1Password
description: Password manager with browser autofill, passkeys and SSH-key agent.
why: Strong unique passwords everywhere; can also store and serve your SSH keys.

name: Notion
description: All-in-one workspace for docs, wikis and project tracking.
why: Popular for team wikis and personal planning.

name: Obsidian
description: Markdown notes stored as local files, with links between notes.
why: Your notes stay as plain files you own; great for a personal knowledge base.

name: The Unarchiver
description: Opens RAR, 7z and many other archive formats.
why: macOS only handles .zip natively.

name: VLC
description: Plays almost any video or audio file.
why: Handles formats QuickTime can't (MKV, AVI, odd codecs).

name: Stats
description: CPU, memory, network and battery stats in the menu bar.
why: See at a glance what is slowing your Mac down.

name: AppCleaner
description: Uninstalls apps together with their leftover files.
why: Dragging an app to the Trash leaves settings and caches behind.

name: Maccy
description: Lightweight clipboard history manager.
why: Paste anything you copied earlier; skip it if you use Raycast's clipboard history.

name: Wispr Flow
description: AI voice dictation that works in any app and tidies up what you say as you go.
why: Speak instead of type for emails, notes, docs and AI prompts; often 3-4x faster than typing. Free tier, paid plan for unlimited use.

name: Spotify
description: Music and podcast streaming.
why: For background music while you work.

name: AWS CLI
description: Official command-line tool for Amazon Web Services.
why: Needed to script or inspect anything in AWS. Configure with: aws configure sso.

name: Google Cloud CLI
description: gcloud, gsutil and bq for Google Cloud.
why: Needed if you work on GCP or BigQuery.

name: Azure CLI
description: The az command for Microsoft Azure.
why: Needed if you work on Azure.

name: Terraform
description: Infrastructure as code: define cloud resources in config files.
why: The most widely used IaC tool. Installed from HashiCorp's official tap.

name: kubectl
description: Command-line tool for Kubernetes clusters.
why: Required for anything Kubernetes.

name: Helm
description: Package manager for Kubernetes.
why: Install and upgrade apps on a cluster from charts.

name: k9s
description: Terminal UI for browsing and managing Kubernetes clusters.
why: Much faster than typing kubectl commands for day-to-day debugging.

name: psql (libpq)
description: PostgreSQL client tools (psql, pg_dump) without running a database server.
why: Connect to Postgres from the terminal. Homebrew doesn't add it to PATH; add /opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin.

name: DBeaver Community
description: Free GUI for almost any SQL database.
why: Browse tables, run queries and view ER diagrams across Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake and more.

name: TablePlus
description: Fast native database GUI (free tier with limits).
why: A lighter, more Mac-like alternative to DBeaver.

name: Miniforge (conda)
description: Minimal conda installer using the community conda-forge channel.
why: Use when you need conda packages (GDAL, CUDA-style stacks); otherwise uv is simpler.

name: JupyterLab
description: Notebook environment for interactive Python and data exploration.
why: Explore data step by step with charts inline. (VS Code can also open notebooks.)

name: DuckDB
description: Fast in-process analytics database: SQL on CSV/Parquet files.
why: Query gigabytes of local files with SQL instantly, no server needed.

name: Figma
description: Collaborative interface design and prototyping.
why: The industry standard for UI design and design handoff.

name: Inkscape
description: Free vector graphics editor.
why: Edit SVGs, logos and illustrations without an Illustrator licence.

name: GIMP
description: Free raster image editor.
why: Photo retouching and image editing without Photoshop.

name: Blender
description: Free 3D modelling, animation and rendering suite.
why: For 3D, motion graphics and product renders.

name: OBS Studio
description: Screen recording and live streaming.
why: Record demos, tutorials and presentations with scenes and overlays.

name: HandBrake
description: Video converter and compressor.
why: Shrink screen recordings before sharing them.

name: ImageOptim
description: Lossless image compression by drag-and-drop.
why: Smaller images for websites and docs without visible quality loss.
